doc.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-10-07

chapter: Touring Alabama and Florida, first New Orleans trips
title: Sadie's boat band and a Mandeville job
summary: Billie struggles to recall the band personnel and tells how Buddy Manaday and Lawrence Toca took her to a Saturday dance in Mandeville.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: So who was in that band with Johnny and all that?

Let me see. Nothing I remember. Let's see. I couldn't remember. Ivory Garner for Pre-Sax. Ain't that what his name? Oh my God. He was playing sax, Chinese. Now them's only two. Let me see. Who else can I think of? Who was the leader? Well, Buddy P.T. was the leader. He played trumpet at that time. He was a trumpet player. That's the only thing I can remember. Buddy and Ivory Garner and Chinese. Them's only one of them.
Them's only one of the bands who played bass?

There was a heavyset dog fella, but I can't think of his name. He's a chunky fat fella, but a real dog. I don't remember. I don't remember. I don't know his name. I don't know his name. He lives on Criot? He did live somewhere back. Doition was. I don't know that man's name was like. He was a barber by Trey. His name was on my tongue right there. I don't know. He'll come to you. We'll ask somebody else. We'll ask somebody else. We'll ask somebody else. I mean, I wasn't, you know, stay here long enough to get reacquainted with him. Like, you know. He was a barber by Trey. I can't call that man heavyset dog fella. Buddy's plays all the time. Me too. I look like I'm looking at him now. Can't call that man's name.
Trying to think of who'd be playing trombone with that band.

Will he playin' drum go? Let me see. Jim Crow. Jim Crow. Let me see what Jim Crow. No, no. Jim Crow. I don't know. I just remember now. Was it Sonny Henry with the. No, this fellow was playing the bass with Sadie, Chinese, Buddy PT. But now. Did he have a banjo player? Johnny, yeah. We didn't see there. No, Johnny. Yeah, that's with Johnny, Johnny, David. You were in that band? No, Johnny was on the boat. Yeah, but Johnny, wait, I'm trying to get that together now. No, Johnny wasn't with them, no.

Seems to me he was probably with Sam Morgan then. I'm trying to remember now. About that time. He and Jim Crow would have been playing with Sam Morgan. Yeah. And uh, did you ever know George Washington?
Yeah. I believe it was his name, George Washington. Did he play bass?
No, he played trombone. Trombone. I knew George Washington.
That might have been George Washington. He was a dog fella. Ain't he?
Ain't George Washington a dog fella? No, I think he was a short fella.

Little short guy, George Washington. George Washington, no. I know George Washington. Let's see. I wonder if it could have been uh... I wasn't Dave the bass player. I wasn't Dave the bass player. I didn't like it, Tommy.
Oh, I don't think so. I don't know. I don't know.
Let's see Duck Ernest play bass. I'm trying to think of who the different guys have played, you know, around with Buddy's gang. Uh, Buddy Manaday. Did you know him?
Buddy Manaday. What do you play, banjo? Buddy Manaday? Yeah, I played with Buddy Manaday. Buddy Manaday. Buddy Manaday. He ain't a slender, slender, slender fella, huh?
Well, I didn't know him. I definitely heard of him.

Buddy Manaday. I called him Buddy Manaday from Manderville. He stayed in Manderville. He played banjo. Yeah. Cause I went over there. Right. I'm telling you, he stayed over Manderville. Well, I'll tell you what happened. When Sadie got able to go back on the boat, where Buddy Manaday and Lawrence Tocco came to see the house of Sadie living on Allen. That's when I was here. And, uh, they wanted Sadie or somebody to do a piano player, understand? So that's when Lawrence and Manaday came over there, and Sadie and I happened to be there. Well, I was gonna leave that Monday going back to Birmingham, but they came that Saturday morning. And, uh, Sadie told them that, uh, she would let me go with them, to play that job over there with them, you see? And, cause I was gonna leave out that Monday. So I went with Lawrence, with Buddy Manaday over in Manderville, where they stay in Manderville 1 over there, where we played out in Covenant over there. So we had Covenant somewhere, you know? For that Saturday night dance.
